clue.text: Sequence of events the book division gives rise to

definitions.meaning: a run of happenings, as in the phrase 'a ... of accidents'
one of the numbered sections a novel is split into

explanation.walkthrough: 'the' and 'gives rise to' only join the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a section of a book, and a connected series of incidents.

clue.text: Opening left to choir and clergy's area

parts.note: an opening is an opportunity, a chance

explanation.surface: Someone describes a gap left for the singers and priests in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a church near the altar reserved for clergy and choir has this name.

clue.text: Change local-born substitute

parts.note: to change something is to alter it
someone born in a place is a native of it

explanation.surface: A team brings on a home-grown replacement player.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternative is something available to take the place of another, a substitute.

clue.text: Row at home making midday meal

parts.note: a row, a petty quarrel, is a tiff
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A domestic argument breaks out while lunch is being made.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglo-Indian usage this word names a light lunch.

clue.text: To transfix with sword needs rehearsal

definitions.meaning: to pierce someone completely with a blade
a practice performance of a show from start to finish

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to skewer, and as a noun it means a complete practice of a play.

clue.text: Polishing fan in front of grate

parts.note: a fan or enthusiast is a buff

indicators.note: the front of the word grate is its first letter

explanation.surface: An enthusiast for fireplaces is shining up the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing a surface to a shine is the same as giving it a polish.

clue.text: Sound athlete breathed hard

indicators.note: the clue says the word for athlete is to be heard, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University

explanation.surface: A runner panted noisily after the race.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is someone chosen to compete for Oxford or Cambridge against the other university.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of a verb meaning to puff out air forcefully, as a tired runner does.

clue.text: Diet obviously requiring little preparation

parts.note: a period of not eating at all needs no cooking; read another way, quick meals served ready to eat

explanation.definitionFit: Burgers and chips served at once need hardly any preparation by the customer, the wry sense being a diet of total abstinence.

clue.text: Mount view no eye-opener

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word eye is to be removed

parts.note: a view or opinion is an idea

explanation.surface: A mountain vista that fails to surprise anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Mount Ida is a mountain in Greek myth, in Crete and in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ida is the famous peak of classical legend, so 'Mount' points to its name.

clue.text: A measure of liquid English put in vessel

indicators.note: E is placed inside the measure

parts.note: a gallon is a unit of liquid volume

explanation.surface: Someone pours a quantity of English beer into a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sailing ship of the sixteenth century is a vessel in the seafaring sense.

clue.text: Feign exploit

definitions.meaning: to pretend or put on a show
a deed or feat, used as a noun

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for pretending and a noun for a deed.

clue.text: Fiddle with seat in church, covering over a nail

parts.note: to fiddle with something is to finger it
a stall is a seat in the choir of a church

explanation.surface: Someone fidgets in their choir pew while a protective sheath covers a nail.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath worn on an injured digit protects it, including the fingernail.

clue.text: Chronic English resort's way along cliff edge

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A dreadful English seaside town has a road along its clifftop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like the seaside town but means re-sort: CHRONIC plus E is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A road built along the face of a cliff, typically above the sea, has this name.

clue.text: Position no longer frozen

parts.note: something cancelled is off, no longer happening
frozen water is ice

explanation.surface: A post or situation that is no longer locked in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A post or role held, such as public office, is a position.

clue.text: Their sister could be a long-haired type

indicators.note: these letters could be rearranged to make something else

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a friend's sibling might have long hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A red gundog breed with a long silky coat is a long-haired type of dog.

clue.text: Cigarette, one of several in the box

definitions.meaning: slang for a smoke, thought to shorten life

definitions.text: one of several in the box
definitions.meaning: a fastener driven into a coffin lid

explanation.definitionFit: Slang term for a cigarette, literally a nail used to close a coffin.

clue.text: Bony heel

definitions.meaning: to heel over is to tilt, as a ship does

explanation.definitionFit: The word means thin as an adjective and to tilt as a verb, like a ship heeling.

clue.text: The power to move a crazy proposal

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A mad idea put to a meeting carries the persuasive force to stir people.
explanation.definitionFit: The faculty of moving from place to place is a dictionary sense of the word.

clue.text: Girls engaged in Eastern cafes to dance

indicators.note: dancing letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Young women in an oriental coffee shop are betrothed and want to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The page reads 'caf', but the letters need CAFES: IN plus E plus CAFES is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who are engaged to be married are fiancées.

clue.text: Swell, being ill internally, is fading away

indicators.note: the illness word sits inside the posh person

parts.note: a swell or toff is a fashionable upper-class person
ailing means being unwell

explanation.surface: A dandy who is unwell inside is slowly declining.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwindling gradually to nothing is the sense of this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Little perch a frog may spring from

parts.note: a tad is a small amount
a perch is an old unit of length, the same as a pole

explanation.surface: A frog leaps off a small branch where it was sitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' is the old length measure (five and a half yards), not a seat or the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogs develop from the larval stage, so it is what a frog grows out of.

clue.text: Run to the front — hear this bird

indicators.note: the last letter, R (run in cricket scoring), runs round to the start of the word hear

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to dash forward and listen to a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flightless South American bird resembling an ostrich.

clue.text: Mark on motorway that means reverse

parts.note: Mark Antony, the Roman general
M is the usual abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A scratch on the motorway signals that traffic should back up.
explanation.definitionFit: A word meaning the opposite of another is one that means its reverse.

clue.text: Fathers, say, absorbed in gambling

indicators.note: one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: bets are wagers, gambling
EG, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: Fathers who are absorbed in betting, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To father children is to beget them; this is the third-person form.

clue.text: Governess expected girl to be backward

parts.note: something due is expected

indicators.note: the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A governess anticipated that her charge would be a slow learner.
explanation.definitionFit: An older woman acting as chaperone and governess to girls in a Spanish household.

clue.text: Concern when one fades away from outbreak of enteritis

indicators.note: an outbreak scatters things, so the letters of enteritis are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Worry when an attack of stomach illness begins to subside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when one fades away from' says I is taken out: ENTERITIS without one I is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To have an interest in something is to be concerned in it.

clue.text: Last two leave photographer's place, making a bolt for it

indicators.note: the final pair of letters is dropped

parts.note: a photographer works in a studio

explanation.surface: Someone flees the photographer's premises once the last two clients leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a bolt for it' suggests escape, but a bolt here is a fastening rivet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a nail or rivet with a large head, a kind of bolt.

clue.text: Score players note

parts.note: an orchestra is a body of players
te is a note in sol-fa

explanation.surface: Musicians write down a figure on a list.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a piece of music is to arrange it for instruments, to orchestrate it.

clue.text: Nothing less than a masterstroke gets the prize

indicators.note: 'less than' here means minus, so the nothing symbol is subtracted from the stroke word

parts.note: a coup is a brilliant stroke
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Anything short of brilliance wins a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy cup is a typical prize in sport.

clue.text: Bark coming from distance

indicators.note: the letters come out of the word distance

explanation.surface: A dog's woof is heard far away.
explanation.walkthrough: Tan is bark from oak used in tanning leather, not a dog's bark.
explanation.definitionFit: Crushed oak bark used for tanning hides is called tan.

clue.text: Former partner pretended to be at mercy of weather

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
one who posed as someone pretended to be them

explanation.surface: An ex-spouse who pretended to be hardy is left out in the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A site open to wind and rain without shelter is unprotected from the elements.

clue.text: Left university to play guitar for several years

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar

explanation.surface: Someone left university to play the guitar for some time.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of five years, from the Roman purification ceremony held every five years.
